subject: Onboarding surge bucket and top-up structure for Neptune Health expansion
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@neptunehealth.com>, Tom Bridges <tom.bridges@neptunehealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding surge bucket and top-up structure for Neptune Health expansion

Hi Lena / Tom,

Great to catch up last week — thanks for sharing the initial traffic projections for the new patient-facing features. Based on the call and the mix of short chat sessions + longer report-generation requests, I sketched two options that should keep latency predictable while limiting your overage risk as you bring new products and teams online:

1) Surge bucket (short-term capacity cushion)
   - 200M token surge bucket to cover onboarding spikes for 90 days
   - Applies only to hosted API endpoints tied to the "mobile-sdk" and "analytics-pipeline" routes
   - Billed monthly as a flat top-up at a reduced blended per-token rate during the 90-day window

2) Incremental commit + pro-rated ramp
   - Commit tier add-on: 3-month incremental commit equal to 25% of your existing monthly committed tokens
   - If usage stays above the incremental commit after month 3, it rolls into the baseline at the agreed discounted rate; otherwise, it expires and you only pay the consumed tokens

Key points: both options include a built-in one-time onboarding credit (equivalent to ~5% of the surge bucket value) to offset test traffic and tuning. We can combine both — e.g., surge bucket up front for the first 60–90 days and an incremental commit for predictable baseline growth.

Attached: a quick model (neptune_topup_modeling.xlsx) with token breakouts and examples for monthly bills under different ramp scenarios.

If this looks reasonable, I can draft a short amendment (1–2 pages) that shows the surge bucket terms + the pro-rating language.

Thanks —
Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: neptune_topup_modeling.xlsx]
From: Lena Park <lena.park@neptunehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding surge bucket and top-up structure for Neptune Health expansion

Diego — thanks for the fast turnaround and the spreadsheet. A few quick clarifying questions before we loop procurement: 

- For the surge bucket: does the reduced blended per-token rate apply only to tokens consumed from the surge bucket, or to all usage during the 90-day window? We need clarity because our finance team treats buckets differently from committed tiers.
- On the incremental commit: how do you calculate the pro-rate if we start the incremental commit mid-billing cycle? Example: we enable on Sept 20.
- If we combine both approaches, will you guarantee that surplus tokens from the surge bucket are consumed before incremental commit tokens are billed? In other words, can the surge bucket act as a buffer first, then the commit covers steady-state?

Also: can you provide the amendment as a track-changes PDF so our legal can redline? Tom (cc'd) will own the procurement thread.

Best,
Lena
Head of Platform, Neptune Health
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Onboarding surge bucket and top-up structure for Neptune Health expansion

Marissa / Priyom — forwarding Lena's clarifying questions. Need your help on two things before I send the amendment back: 

1) Pricing behavior (Priyom): please confirm how billing order works if a customer has both a surge bucket and an incremental commit. We prefer to have surge bucket tokens drawn first (to protect customer from immediate commit charges), but need to confirm any internal limitations with how the hosted meter aggregates across routes. Also confirm the blended per-token example I used in the spreadsheet if the surge bucket is used: should the surge-bucket consumption be billed at the surge rate only, or should all usage during the 90-day window reflect a blended adjustment?

2) Contract language (Marissa): can you draft a 1–2 page amendment that:
   - defines surge bucket (scope: routes, time window, non-transferrable)
   - states the pro-rate method if commit begins mid-cycle (pro-rate by calendar days in cycle)
   - ordering: surge bucket is consumed before incremental commit tokens; any leftover surge tokens are non-refundable and will expire at the end of the window unless rolled into a new commit

Budget sensitivity: Neptune signaled they want predictable cost for Q4 operator budgets. If we propose a blended rate for the surge bucket that is materially lower than the incremental commit rate, we should get approval for the margin delta.

I'll aim to send Lena a draft by EOD.

Diego
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@neptunehealth.com>, Tom Bridges <tom.bridges@neptunehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding surge bucket and top-up structure for Neptune Health expansion

Lena / Tom — thanks for the quick questions. Attached is a draft amendment (proposed-amendment_v2.pdf) that incorporates the behaviors we discussed and the pro-rate language. Summary of the answers inline below: 

- Surge bucket billing: tokens drawn from the surge bucket are billed at the surge rate. We do not retroactively re-price all other usage during the 90-day window. This keeps accounting simple and ensures the burst protection is a discrete purchase.
- Pro-rate if starting mid-cycle: we pro-rate the incremental commit by calendar days in the billing cycle (example included in the amendment). If you enable on Sept 20 in a 30-day cycle starting Sept 1, you pay 11/30 of the first month's commit fee.
- Consumption order: surge bucket tokens will be consumed first for eligible routes. Once the surge bucket is exhausted or expired, consumption falls back to committed tokens, then overage pricing. Leftover surge tokens are non-refundable and may be credited toward an extension or rolled into a new commit at a discounted conversion rate (see section 2.b).

Next steps:
- I attached the amendment as a PDF with tracked language so legal can redline. [Attachment: proposed-amendment_v2.pdf]
- If procurement wants numbers for the blended vs. surge-rate margin, Marissa / Priyom are looped to provide the finance impact.

If this captures what you need, let me know and I'll send the formal DocuSign link.

Best,
Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
